sport_profiles.planning_summary: Badminton is a high-speed racket sport requiring split-step timing, multidirectional footwork, lunge/deceleration capacity, overhead shoulder durability, racket touch, serve/receive skill, singles/doubles tactical awareness, and repeat high-intensity rally recovery.
training_priorities: split-step timing, first step, lunge, and recovery to base
clear, drop, smash, drive, lift, block, and net-shot skill
singles rally construction or doubles rotation based on role
shoulder/scapular, trunk, calf/Achilles, knee, and ankle durability
reactive agility and repeat high-intensity effort capacity
do_not_pair: high-volume multi-shuttle lunges with knee, shin, Achilles, or ankle symptoms
smash-volume spikes with shoulder or low-back symptoms
new plyometrics and high tournament/match density
heavy lower-body eccentric work immediately before important matches
fatigue-first agility before footwork quality is stable
progression_guardrails: progress footwork complexity before footwork speed
progress stroke volume before power volume
use 24-hour knee, ankle, Achilles, shoulder, and back response before adding court load
separate high-impact multi-shuttle work from heavy lower-body S&C
make tactics format-specific: singles, doubles, mixed doubles, front/rear court

stage_0_medical_and_symptom_control.goal: Control pain, swelling, irritability, and basic daily function before badminton-specific loading.

stage_1_capacity_rebuild.goal: Restore local strength, mobility, balance, and trunk control without chaotic court demand.
stage_1_capacity_rebuild.court_exposure: basic shadow movement, no maximal lunges, no max smashes, no reactive play

stage_2_controlled_footwork_and_hitting.goal: Reintroduce planned badminton patterns at low to moderate intensity.
court_exposure: limited controlled smashes if shoulder/back tolerant

stage_3_integrated_drills.goal: Blend movement and hitting with moderate reactivity while controlling volume.

stage_4_practice_participation.goal: Return to normal practice with exposure caps and no competition density.

stage_5_match_exposure.goal: Return to competition in managed dose.

stage_6_return_to_performance.goal: Restore pre-injury or target performance load, tournament density, and high-intensity skill execution.
court_exposure: tournament density only after repeat tolerance

beginner.court_load: short technical blocks, planned footwork, low-volume lunges, controlled overheads, low-amplitude hops.
beginner.snc: bodyweight strength, balance, trunk control, calf raises, shoulder/scapular basics, landing and braking mechanics.

intermediate.primary_goal: Specific capacity with controlled exposure progression.
intermediate.court_load: tracked lunge and smash blocks, progressive jump landing, moderate multishuttle, planned match play.
intermediate.snc: progressive lower-body strength, unilateral strength, deceleration, lateral power, trunk rotation control, cuff/scapular and forearm work.
avoid: heavy eccentric lower body before match

advanced.primary_goal: High specific tolerance and performance repeatability.
advanced.court_load: individualized smash, lunge, jump, rally, and tournament exposure based on history and readiness.
advanced.snc: strength and power maintenance, microdosed plyometrics, individualized tendon and shoulder durability, high-quality deceleration and reactive work.
avoid: novel soreness-producing gym blocks in competition weeks

sport_training_rules.rule: Separate the problem into ready position, grip, racket preparation, backswing or hold, forward swing, contact, follow-through, and recovery. sport_teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Develop badminton_model_racket_preparation for a intermediate badminton player.
prerequisites: basic strokes and footwork are repeatable
can recover to base under simple pressure
teaching_priorities: Use a ready racket that can move to forecourt, midcourt, or rear-court contact quickly. Preparation changes by stroke: compact and in front for drives and blocks, early shoulder turn and racket set for overheads, soft high racket presentation for net, and stable setup for serve.
Default ready position keeps the racket in front of the trunk with the head above hand height where practical; avoid resting the racket low after each shot.
progression_signals: movement quality does not collapse under fatigue
recovers to base or partner shape

sport_teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Develop badminton_model_low_backhand_serve for a beginner badminton player.
prerequisites: safe basic movement
can hold racket and make simple contact
no sharp court-movement pain
teaching_priorities: Set a stable legal stance, hold shuttle consistently in front, use a short controlled backswing, move the racket continuously forward, contact the shuttle cleanly below the legal height, and send a flat-low trajectory that falls near the receiver's service line.
Thumb or bevel-based backhand grip, racket face slightly open enough to clear the tape without popping the shuttle high.
progression_signals: movement quality does not collapse under fatigue

sport_teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Develop badminton_model_flick_and_high_serve for a beginner badminton player.
prerequisites: safe basic movement
can hold racket and make simple contact
no sharp court-movement pain
teaching_priorities: The flick serve starts like the low serve and adds late acceleration to send the shuttle over the receiver. The high forehand serve uses a larger underarm action and higher trajectory to push the receiver deep, mainly in singles and early learning contexts.
Flick serve must hide intent through similar setup to the low serve. High serve uses relaxed underarm rhythm, stable base, and upward racket path.
progression_signals: movement quality does not collapse under fatigue

sport_teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Develop badminton_model_overhead_clear for a beginner badminton player.
prerequisites: safe basic movement
can hold racket and make simple contact
no sharp court-movement pain
teaching_priorities: Use early shoulder turn, high contact in front or slightly above the hitting shoulder, whole-chain acceleration, and a full enough follow-through to send the shuttle high and deep. Defensive clears buy time; attacking or punch clears travel flatter and faster when contact quality allows.
Racket set behind and above the shoulder with non-racket arm helping alignment; grip relaxed until acceleration.
progression_signals: movement quality does not collapse under fatigue

sport_teaching_progressions.learning_goal: Develop badminton_model_overhead_drop for a beginner badminton player.
prerequisites: safe basic movement
can hold racket and make simple contact
no sharp court-movement pain
teaching_priorities: Begin like an overhead clear or smash, then reduce racket speed, change face angle, or add slice to send the shuttle downward into the forecourt. Quality depends on early preparation, high contact, touch, and recovery rather than deceleration that telegraphs the shot too soon.
Show similar rear-court preparation to clear and smash; keep the option to hit straight, cross, fast, slow, sliced, or reverse-sliced drops.
progression_signals: movement quality does not collapse under fatigue

can hold racket and make simple contact
no sharp court-movement pain
teaching_priorities: Create a steep powerful downward stroke from high contact in front, using coordinated trunk, shoulder, elbow, forearm, wrist, and finger acceleration. The aim is not only speed; placement, angle, recovery, and ability to follow the smash matter.
Rear-court preparation should initially resemble clear and drop. Contact should be far enough in front to hit down without excessive lumbar extension.
